sections.title: AI Adoption in Organizations
sections.description: Many organizations now have capable AI tools, but far fewer have turned them into lasting value. The obstacles are often organizational rather than technical: unclear strategy, unprepared workforces, weak governance, and no shared way to measure success. This course treats AI adoption as a problem of organizational change. Drawing on organizational dynamics, anthropology, and science and technology studies, students examine how AI, including increasingly autonomous agents, reshapes work, expertise, and decision-making. Students learn to assess an organization’s AI maturity, diagnose why initiatives stall, and design governance and change approaches that fit their context. They also practice applied research, pairing in-depth interviews with digital methods. Each student leaves with an evidence-based adoption plan for an AI initiative in their own organization or field.
